Exclusion criteria are methodological rules used to define which patients or cases are removed from the calculation of specific healthcare quality indicators. These criteria ensure that performance metrics accurately reflect the quality of care and are not skewed by cases where the intended clinical pathway could not be completed, or where the outcome is determined by factors outside the specific scope of the indicator being measured.

In the provided documentation, a specific exclusion criterion is defined for [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]]. Patients who die during their primary admission are excluded from the calculation of this indicator [^src1]. By removing these cases, the metric focuses only on the patient population that survives the initial hospitalization, ensuring the indicator evaluates the intended clinical outcomes or processes exclusively for those who are eligible for the subsequent care being measured.

## Claims
- Patienter, som dør under den primære indlæggelse, ekskluderes fra beregningen af indikator 8 [^src1] (indikator-8)
